newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares jump 2.56 pct on new govt hopes.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares jump 2.56 pct on new govt hopes.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued their sharp rise on Friday amid new coalition prospects which flared after the resignation of the Islamist-led coalition government late on Wednesday brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,642, up 41 points, or 2.56 percent from Thursday when it gained 2.3 percent. Trade volume jumped further to 27.12 trillion lira ($185.9 million) from 17.83 trillion ($122.2 million).

"The market bought on expectations that Mesut Yilmaz would be asked to set up a new government. It is obvious that the market will welcome such a development if it becomes true," said Cem Baycan from Delta securities.
President Suleyman Demirel invited main opposition Motherland Party leader Mesut Yilmaz to his residence late on Friday amid speculation he would be asked to head a new government.
Yilmaz is one of the favourites to be appointed by Demirel as prime minister-designate following the resignation of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

Yilmaz has earlier said he would exclude the Islamist Welfare Party and seek an alliance with two leftist opposition parties and the other conservative True Path Party which has been the junior coalition partner in the past one year.
However Yilmaz, a former prime minister, could have trouble finding the parliamentary majority needed to approve any government he could set up.
